observation_summary: The PiePlot class throws an exception when drawing a chart with a null dataset because it attempts to access the dataset without checking for nullity.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces two null checks for the 'dataset' field. In the first instance (getMaximumExplodePercent), it returns a default value (0.0) if the dataset is null. In the second instance (in the state initialization), it wraps the dataset processing in a null check to prevent a NullPointerException. These are classic 'Checking' defects where missing validation of data leads to runtime errors.
evidence_used: The fix adds 'if (this.dataset == null) { return 0.0; }' in getMaximumExplodePercent.
The fix adds 'if (this.dataset != null) { ... }' around the dataset processing in the state initialization.
The trigger test 'testDrawWithNullDataset' confirms the failure occurs when the dataset is null.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix does not change the underlying algorithm or logic; it merely adds conditional checks to handle a null input state safely.
